articles.title: Galo da Madrugada homenageia caboclo de lança no carnaval de 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Tema do desfile, que acontece em 6 de fevereiro, é 'Ao canto do Galo, a espora é a lança'. Prévias do maior bloco do mundo também foram anunciadas nesta quarta-feira (7).
articles.summary: Tema do desfile, que acontece em 6 de fevereiro, é 'Ao canto do Galo, a espora é a lança'. Prévias do maior bloco do mundo também foram anunciadas nesta quarta-feira (7).
articles.body:
O desfile do Galo da Madrugada no carnaval de 2027 vai homenagear o caboclo de lança do maracatu rural ( veja vídeo acima ). Com o tema “Ao canto do Galo, a espora é a lança”, o maior bloco do mundo vai reverenciar a cultura popular da Zona da Mata Norte de Pernambuco. O anúncio foi feito nesta quarta-feira (7), na sede da agremiação, no bairro de São José, no Centro do Recife .

O bloco desfila no Sábado de Zé Pereira que, em 2027, será no dia 6 de fevereiro. Para o criador e presidente do Galo da Madrugada, Rômulo Menezes, o tema escolhido reconhece a importância cultural das regiões dos canaviais e do trabalho exercido pelos canavieiros do interior pernambucano.

“É uma homenagem bastante justa, não apenas pelo lado cultural, folclórico, mas também pelo lado da labuta que eles [os canavieiros] têm, em cortar cana debaixo de um sol escaldante, mas mantendo o trabalho e a cultura, e nós respeitamos muito isso”, disse, emocionado, Rômulo Menezes.

Desde 2014, o caboclo de lança é reconhecido como Patrimônio Cultural Imaterial do Brasil pelo Instituto do Patrimônio Histórico e Artístico Nacional (Iphan). Conhecido como Mestre Barachinha, Manoel Carlos é líder do Maracatu Estrela Dourada, do município de Buenos Aires , na Zona da Mata Norte de Pernambuco , e ficou grato com a homenagem do Galo da Madrugada.

“Todos os caboclos de laça do mundo serão homenageados no maior bloco do mundo. [...] O maracatu de baque solto é cultura nobre, mantida por gente pobre, então a gente luta e tira de onde não tem, mas temos o prazer de festejar uma homenagem dessas”, contou o mestre.

Tatyana Veríssimo, diretora de projetos do Galo da Madrugada, destacou a importância dessa homenagem. “A figura do caboclo de lança vai representar também todos os fazedores da cultura, todas as pessoas que trabalham para preservar a nossa cultura e a transmissão de saberes, até para uma nova geração”, afirmou.

O tema escolhido busca preservar as histórias, os artistas e as manifestações do maracatu rural, também chamado de maracatu de baque solto.

"O caboclo de lança é o guardião dos saberes, da cultura, da sustentabilidade e das matas. Ele é o trabalhador rural que, ao mesmo tempo, é o artesão que faz suas roupas coloridas", disse Francisco Câmara, carnavalesco e diretor de Fantasias do Galo da Madrugada.

Caboclo de lança do maracatu rural é homenageado pelo Galo da Madrugada no desfile do carnaval de 2027 — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

As prévias do Galo da Madrugada começam no dia 22 de outubro, com a tradicional “Quinta no Galo”. As apresentações seguem até o mês de janeiro de 2027, com a seguinte programação:

28 de janeiro: Maestro Forró e Orquestra Popular da Bomba do Hemetério.

A "Quinta no Galo" acontece na sede do Galo da Madrugada, localizada no número 984 da Rua da Concórdia, no bairro de São José, no Centro do Recife. Os shows começam a partir das 20h. Os ingressos custam R$ 60 (inteira) e R$ 30 (meia), à venda no local e na internet .

Em três sábados de janeiro (dias 9, 16 e 23), vão ser realizados os "Ensaios de Carnaval", comandados pelo Bloco das Ilusões e pelo cantor André Rio. O Galo da Madrugada ainda não divugou a programação nem os valores dos ingressos.

Fundado em 1978, o Galo da Madrugada se tornou Patrimônio Cultural Imaterial de Pernambuco em 2009;

Em 1994, entrou para o Guinness Book como o maior bloco de carnaval do mundo;

Em 2026, o bloco levou cerca de 2,5 milhões de pessoas para o desfile, com o tema "Frevo no Planeta Galo", sobre sustentabilidade, preservação ambiental e conscientização ecológica.

* Estagiária sob a supervisão do editor Bruno Marinho.

articles.title: Marco Antonio de Paula: o candidato que usou 10 nomes em 10 eleições | G1
articles.standfirst: Marco Antonio de Paula, que usou na urna "Pastor Marco Antonio" neste ano, tentou se eleger deputado federal e obteve 38 votos.
articles.summary: Marco Antonio de Paula foi o candidato a deputado federal menos votado na região de Campinas após usar dez nomes diferentes em dez eleições.
articles.body:
Candidato a deputado da região de Campinas com menos votos em 2026, Marco Antonio de Paula já disputou 10 eleições com nomes de urna diferentes — Foto: Reprodução/TSE

Aos 55 anos, Marco Antonio de Paula passou os últimos 22 anos tentando um cargo eletivo na política. Menos votado entre todos os candidatos a deputado federal com atuação na região de Campinas (SP) em 2026, já disputou 10 eleições, e a cada nova tentativa, usou um nome de urna diferente. Em nenhuma, no entanto, foi eleito.

Desta vez, exibiu o nome de Pastor Marco Antônio, recebendo 38 votos na disputa por uma vaga à Câmara dos Deputados em Brasília (DF). Veja, abaixo, a relação dos cinco candidatos com atuação na região menos votados nas Eleições 2026.

Agora "pastor", Marco Antonio já esteve identificado nas urnas como "Perna De Pau" ou "Capivara" , além de variações desses apelidos.

⚠️ "Capivara" , aliás, é o mais frequente deles, e pelo qual ficou conhecido na região, em especial em Americana (SP), onde foi processado por estelionato , praticado 30 vezes, e condenado em 2015. A pena foi totalmente cumprida em março de 2021 .

Dados do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) mostram que a Procuradoria Regional Eleitoral apresentou impugnação ao registro de Marco Antonio de Paula, que entrou com recurso, e por isso pode concorrer ao pleito.

O levantamento mostra ainda que ele foi já foi condenado outra vez e respondeu a processos:

Condenado por contravenção penal em Americana, com pena extinta em 2011;

Respondeu a dois processos por ameaça em Andradina (SP), ambos encerrados em 2001 por decadência e extinção da punibilidade.

Respondeu a dois processos de trânsito e contravenção em Araçatuba (SP), ambos extintos nos anos 1990.

A ligação com Americana inclui ainda um período como servidor comissionado na Secretaria de Obras e Serviços Urbanos, em 2011, durante a gestão de Diego De Nadai. Procurado, o ex-prefeito não quis se manifestar.

"Capivara" também já esteve envolvido em uma ocorrência relacionada a invasão de terra em Santo Antônio de Posse (SP), em 2016 . O grupo fazia parte de uma associação ligada a Marco Antônio.

O g1 tentou contato com Marco Antonio de Paula pelas redes sociais e também pelo partido Avante, mas não recebeu resposta até esta publicação.

Dez eleições, dez nomes, nove partidos...

Marco Antonio de Paula já participou de dez eleições desde 2004, sendo o único hiato entre os pleitos de 2018 e 2020. Já nas eleições de 2016, 2022 e 204, foi considerado inapto ou teve o registro anulado pela Justiça Eleitoral.

A maior votação foi obtida em 2014, quando, concorrendo como "Marco Antonio - O Capivara", recebeu 1.841 votos para deputado estadual e ficou entre os suplentes do partido.

Na ocasião ele estava filiado ao PR, atualmente o PL. O partido, aliás, foi o único pelo qual disputou duas eleições (concorreu a vereador em 2012). Ao todo, esteve em nove legendas diferentes. Veja:

O Pastor Marco Antonio foi o candidato a deputado federal com atuação na região de Campinas com o menor número de votos em 2026.

Ao todo, os cinco com pior desempenho nas urnas somaram 659 votos.

Para efeito de comparação, a candidata a deputada federal eleita com a menor votação em 2026 foi Sônia Guajajara (Psol), com 54.207 votos.

Já na disputa para deputado ou deputada estadual, Domingos Honorato (DC) obteve 29 votos - menos que Capivara, mas a candidatura dele é considerada "anulada sub judice" pelo TSE.

articles.title: Hotéis para eventos e hospedagem em Foz do Iguaçu | G1
articles.standfirst: De grandes congressos a encontros corporativos, o destino oferece espaços, hospedagem e estrutura para diferentes necessidades.
articles.summary: De grandes congressos a encontros corporativos, o destino oferece espaços, hospedagem e estrutura para diferentes necessidades.
articles.body:
O sucesso na organização de congressos, convenções ou treinamentos corporativos depende diretamente da escolha adequada das salas e da acomodação para os participantes. Foz do Iguaçu simplifica consideravelmente essa logística.

Reconhecida pela ICCA (International Congress and Convention Association) como uma das cidades brasileiras que mais recebe eventos internacionais, o Destino Iguaçu apresenta infraestrutura hoteleira robusta. Atualmente, dos 32 meios de hospedagem associados ao Visit Iguassu, 16 dispõem de centro de convenções ou salas estruturadas para eventos. As opções variam de espaços boutique para reuniões intimistas até complexos com capacidade para mais de 4.000 pessoas simultaneamente.

Portanto, organizadores de congressos, convenções e treinamentos encontram no destino uma solução completa, com opções de hotéis com e sem salas de eventos para diferentes tipos de eventos e perfis de público.

Por que considerar Foz do Iguaçu para sediar um evento?

Antes de definir a sede, é essencial compreender o que faz da cidade um polo no turismo de negócios (MICE). Localizada na fronteira trinacional entre Brasil, Argentina e Paraguai, a cidade garante excelente conectividade aérea, recebendo voos regulares diretos das principais capitais do Brasil e de grandes centros da América do Sul.

A hotelaria voltada a eventos está estrategicamente distribuída em três eixos principais:

Corredor turístico (Avenida das Cataratas): concentra os grandes resorts e complexos de convenções.

Região central: ideal para fácil acesso ao comércio urbano, abrigando opções práticas de médio e pequeno porte.

BR-277: principal acesso rodoviário, abrigando estruturas amplas e integradas à natureza.

Confira este vídeo sobre a estrutura de eventos em Foz do Iguaçu e apresenta os motivos pelos quais a cidade conta com uma ampla infraestrutura para eventos:

Quais hotéis oferecem centro de convenções?

Ao alinhar o porte do seu evento com a estrutura local, você garante maior conforto e assertividade. Abaixo, detalhamos os empreendimentos com foco em eventos.

Grandes Complexos para Congressos e Convenções

Ideais para eventos que exigem múltiplos ambientes ou grandes plenárias, estes locais oferecem metragens e capacidades expressivas:

Bourbon Thermas Eco Resort Cataratas do Iguaçu: Conta com 15 salas distribuídas em 5.200 m², abrigando até 4.000 participantes. Destaque sustentável, é o primeiro resort da região com o selo Eco Responsável.

Grand Carimã Resort & Convention Center: Apresenta uma área total de eventos de 7.000 m². Com 20 salas, sua capacidade somada supera 10.000 pessoas.

Hotel Golden Park Internacional Foz & Convenções by Nacional Inn: No centro da cidade e a 9 km do aeroporto, acomoda até 3.500 pessoas em seus 12 ambientes.

Interludium Iguassu Convention Hotel: Cercado por área verde, o salão comporta até 700 pessoas em auditório e atende coquetéis para 1.000 convidados.

Mabu Thermas Grand Resort: Oferta 10.000 m² de área de eventos, tendo o Salão Brasil como carro-chefe para até 2.700 pessoas em auditório.

Rafain Palace Hotel & Convention: Situado no corredor turístico, opera o maior complexo do destino (18.000 m²). Unindo o Expocenter I e II, chega a 4.400 pessoas em formato auditório, distribuídas em até 44 ambientes.

Recanto Cataratas Thermas Resort & Convention: Possui dois complexos moduláveis. O salão principal suporta mais de 4.500 convidados em formato ballroom com pé-direito de 8 metros.

Wish Foz do Iguaçu Resort: Fica a 9 minutos do aeroporto. Seus salões moduláveis somam 705 m² e atendem 665 pessoas em formato auditório.

Congresso Bras de Cirurgia Bariátrica e Metabólica. — Foto: Visit Iguassu/Divulgação.

Para encontros executivos, treinamentos e boards, opções mais intimistas estão disponíveis:

DoubleTree by Hilton Foz do Iguaçu: No corredor turístico (ao lado do Catuaí Shopping), suas salas atendem até 100 pessoas, ideal para reuniões corporativas menores e diretorias.

Hotel das Cataratas, A Belmond Hotel: Experiência premium dentro do Parque Nacional. As salas Iguaçu e Dom Pedro acomodam 180 participantes.

Hotel Foz do Iguaçu: No coração comercial da cidade, com versatilidade para até 200 pessoas em auditório.

JL Hotel by Bourbon: Estrutura moderna no centro (em frente ao shopping), fornecendo três salas para até 300 pessoas.

Viale Cataratas Hotel & Eventos: Na Avenida das Cataratas, oferece salas moduláveis que acomodam até 500 convidados no formato auditório.

Viale Tower Hotel: Na Via Gastronômica, dispõe de sala para 150 convidados com vista privilegiada da região trinacional.

Wyndham Golden Foz Suítes: Localizado no centro, dispõe de sete salas de eventos para até 280 pessoas em auditório e quatro salas de reuniões que, integradas, somam até 500 participantes.

Congresso Bras de Zoologia e Conferência da Zoologia na Indústria. — Foto: Visit Iguassu/Divulgação.

Hospedagem complementar: opções sem centro de eventos

Nem todo participante opta por estar hospedado no hotel-sede do evento. Ao pensar na organização de um evento, contar com hotéis distribuídos pelas principais regiões da cidade e que atendam com qualidade os diferentes perfis de participantes é um diferencial. Abaixo hotéis associados ao Visit Iguassu sem salas de eventos que podem completar a lista de estabelecimentos indicados para hospedagem durante um evento em Foz do Iguaçu:

Ibis Foz do Iguaçu. — Foto: Ibis Foz do Iguaçu/Divulgação.

Como essas opções ficam espalhadas pelas principais regiões de Foz do Iguaçu, o deslocamento até o hotel-sede costuma ser rápido, o que simplifica a logística de transporte dos participantes.

Como a infraestrutura de Foz do Iguaçu se adapta a diversos formatos de eventos

A mescla de grandes complexos de convenções, espaços boutique e uma oferta hoteleira em variadas categorias confere a Foz do Iguaçu a versatilidade necessária para sediar simultaneamente congressos internacionais, viagens de incentivo, treinamentos corporativos e convenções de vendas.

Dessa forma, profissionais de eventos e agências encontram a facilidade de estruturar uma experiência integral — que engloba estadia, locação de salas, fornecedores especializados, gastronomia e roteiros turísticos — de maneira fluida e sem a necessidade de extensos traslados entre os pontos da cidade.

O time do Visit Iguassu oferece suporte especializado na captação do seu evento, conectando sua empresa a uma ampla rede de associados locais que fornecem serviços dedicados ao setor.

Entre em contato com o Visit Iguassu e descubra tudo o que a região pode proporcionar para o sucesso do seu projeto.

articles.title: Porsche foca no segmento de luxo para elevar margem de lucro | G1
articles.standfirst: Fabricante prevê vender menos carros e aposta em modelos de luxo, como o 911, para recuperar a margem de lucro.
articles.summary: A Porsche reestrutura seus negócios focando em carros de luxo e na redução de custos para recuperar a margem de lucro após queda nas vendas globais.
articles.body:
A Porsche está reestruturando seus negócios para um futuro com vendas menores. A fabricante de carros esportivos aposta em um maior foco nos modelos de luxo para recuperar suas margens de lucro, mesmo diante de uma demanda mais fraca.

A empresa deve, portanto, focar em modelos e versões mais caras dentro do portfólio, como, por exemplo, o icônico 911. Modelos que brigam em segmentos mais concorridos, como os SUV Macan e Cayenne, além dos esportivos com motor 2.0 718 Boxster e 718 Cayman, ficariam com menos atençã.

A montadora, que, assim como sua controladora Volkswagen, passa por uma grande reestruturação para enfrentar vendas fracas e custos elevados, afirmou em seu plano de recuperação que pretende reduzir para menos de 200 mil o número de carros que precisa vender para equilibrar as contas.

O número fica bem abaixo das 279.449 unidades entregues no ano passado .

As entregas globais da Porsche já caíram quase 10% desde 2022 , ano em que a empresa abriu seu capital. A queda na demanda na China e as tarifas impostas pelos Estados Unidos afetaram dois dos principais mercados da marca.

Porsche 911 Turbo S no autódromo Velocitta em Mogi Guaçu (SP). — Foto: Divulgação / Porsche

Durante um evento para investidores no centro de desenvolvimento da empresa, em Weissach, o presidente-executivo Michael Leiters buscou convencer os investidores de que o foco em carros esportivos de luxo, como o 911, pode colocar a Porsche de volta nos trilhos .

A estratégia inclui aumentar os preços dos 10 mil veículos mais caros da marca.

“Queremos reforçar a Porsche como a fabricante de carros esportivos mais cobiçada do mundo”, disse Leiters, colocando a marca ao lado da Ferrari e da Louis Vuitton em termos de valor.

Retorno rápido às margens de dois dígitos

Leiters, que assumiu o cargo no início do ano com a missão de reestruturar a empresa, afirmou que a estratégia, neste momento, será concentrada na redução de custos.

“Não sabemos como será a próxima crise nem de onde ela virá. É por isso que a Porsche precisa ser adaptável, eficiente e resiliente”, disse.

A Porsche estabeleceu uma meta de longo prazo de margem operacional de 15%. No médio prazo, em cerca de cinco anos, a expectativa é chegar a uma margem entre 10% e 15%.

A margem de lucro da empresa despencou no ano passado para 1,1%, muito abaixo dos cerca de 15% registrados quando a Porsche abriu o capital, há quatro anos, sob a liderança de Oliver Blume. Ele deixou o comando da fabricante, mas continua como presidente-executivo da Volkswagen.

Os investidores pareceram receber bem a nova estratégia. As ações da Porsche subiram 3,2% após o anúncio.

articles.title: Mulheres defendem renunciar ao voto e delegá-los aos homens nos EUA | G1
articles.standfirst: Movimento ultraconservador prega a submissão feminina e o 'voto por domicílio' às vésperas das eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA.
articles.summary: Movimento ultraconservador prega a submissão feminina e o 'voto por domicílio' às vésperas das eleições de meio de mandato nos EUA.
articles.body:
Influenciadora digital conservadora norte-americana Savannah Stone, de 21 anos. — Foto: Reprodução/redes sociais

Discussões sobre o antifeminismo defendido por mulheres têm dominado as redes sociais desde o segundo turno das eleições, no último domingo (4). O assunto ganhou fôlego após a eleição de Eduarda Campopiano - a deputada estadual mais votada em São Paulo que se classifica como "inimiga das feministas".

Pode parecer novidade por aqui, mas esse movimento já vem acontecendo há meses nos Estados Unidos .

A menos de um mês das eleições que definirão a composição do Congresso americano e os governadores de 34 estados, uma legião de americanas está disposta a renunciar ao direito de votar e delegá-lo aos maridos .

Com 800 mil seguidores, a influenciadora digital Savannah Stone, de 21 anos, lidera um movimento que propaga a submissão feminina e o voto familiar — apenas um por domicílio e decidido pelo chefe da família.

A tese antifeminista contradiz frontalmente o direito sufragista, conquistado a duras penas em 1920, com a ratificação da 19ª Emenda à Constituição. Mas ganha força no país conservador remodelado na eleição de 2024, que conduziu novamente Donald Trump à Casa Branca.

Casada há dois anos, Stone foi a oradora principal da Cúpula de Liderança Feminina realizada em junho no Texas pelo grupo ultraconservador Turning Point USA, que congrega a juventude pró-MAGA ("Façam os EUA Grandes Novamente", na tradução em português).

O fundador da Turning Point, Charles Kirk, assassinado no ano passado, incentivava as mulheres a buscarem “um diploma de esposa”. Após a sua morte, foi substituído pela viúva, Erika, que recruta jovens para o movimento de direita cristã.

“O feminismo é a maior mentira que já nos contaram enquanto mulheres. É um movimento financiado pelas pessoas mais ricas e perversas com o objetivo de destruir o casamento e a família”, afirmou Savannah Stone.

Ela dirige a comunidade online The Submissive Society, na qual ensina as mulheres a se comportarem diante dos maridos , ao estilo de uma dona de casa tradicional dos anos 1950. Ou seja, é uma empreendedora do antifeminismo.

Num dos vídeos que viralizaram, ela indaga: “Você já tentou usar um vestido de verão e preparar a comida favorita dele? Você já tentou realmente ouvi-lo quando ele fala? Já tentou ficar feliz e contente quando ele chega em casa, em vez de ficar reclamando? Já tentou manter a casa limpa para que seja um santuário para ele voltar e não mais um caos?”

Stone assegura que abriria mão do direito de voto sem hesitar e o fará no próximo mês, nas eleições de meio de mandato. Ela integrou a campanha para a reeleição de Trump, mas admite que se decepcionou. "Ele deu a entender que tudo ia ficar mais acessível; agora a economia está pior. Ele prometeu que não haveria mais guerras no Oriente Médio e estamos em guerra.”

A influenciadora advoga pela ideia de “uma família, um voto” e pela abolição da 19ª Emenda Constitucional, que privaria as mulheres do seu direito de participar do processo democrático. Para a mudança ser aprovada, seria necessário o apoio de dois terços do Congresso e de três quartos dos estados americanos.

Secretário de Guerra dos Estados Unidos, Pete Hegseth, em evento na base naval de Quantico, na Virgínia, em 30 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Evan Vucci/Pool

Pode-se dizer que a tese da revogação do voto feminino também chegou ao Pentágono. O teólogo e pastor Doug Wilson, que dirige a Comunhão de Igrejas Evangélicas Reformadas, é um de seus propagadores mais contundentes e mentor do secretário de Defesa, Pete Hegseth.

Nacionalista cristão, o pastor celebrou em fevereiro um culto no Pentágono, levado pelo controverso Hegseth, assíduo frequentador de sua congregação em Washington.

Wilson propõe para o país o sistema de votação utilizado em seu império religioso , com 170 congregações: o voto é por domicílio e as mulheres só votariam se fossem chefes de família. O voto das solteiras poderia ser substituído pelo de irmãos ou tios. Por enquanto, trata-se de uma tese marginal, mas que é ecoada com veemência em ambientes ultraconservadores.

articles.title: Rua do Congresso em Manaus tem sentido invertido por 10 dias | G1
articles.standfirst: Mudança será mantida até 16 de outubro, das 7h às 18h, para avaliar uma alternativa de circulação e reduzir conflitos no trânsito da região.
articles.summary: A Rua do Congresso em Manaus terá sentido invertido até 16 de outubro para testes do IMMU que visam reduzir conflitos no trânsito do Centro.
articles.body:
Rua do Congresso tem sentido invertido no Centro de Manaus por 10 dias durante teste — Foto: Arielle Lorena/Semcom

A Prefeitura de Manaus iniciou, nesta quarta-feira (7), um teste para inverter temporariamente o sentido de circulação na Rua do Congresso , no Centro. A mudança será mantida até 16 de outubro, das 7h às 18h , para avaliar uma alternativa de circulação e reduzir conflitos no trânsito da região .

Durante o teste, motoristas que estiverem na Rua Monsenhor Coutinho poderão acessar a Rua do Congresso à direita e seguir em direção à Avenida Ramos Ferreira. Atualmente, o fluxo ocorre no sentido contrário.

Segundo o Instituto Municipal de Mobilidade Urbana (IMMU), a alteração também está relacionada à interdição permanente de um trecho da Rua Ferreira Pena, onde será implantada a primeira Rua Gastronômica de Manaus.

"Essa intervenção vai durar dez dias. A ideia é avaliar o fluxo no período de pico, uma vez que, na saída da Eduardo Ribeiro, nós temos aproximadamente 2.200 carros no horário de pico. Com isso, a gente dá uma alternativa para reduzir esse conflito com a Eduardo Ribeiro, e o motorista vai poder pegar aqui a rua do Congresso", explicou o diretor-presidente do IMMU, Elson Andrade.

Agentes do IMMU acompanham o trânsito durante o período de teste e vão coletar dados para avaliar os efeitos da mudança. A Prefeitura orienta os motoristas a ficarem atentos à sinalização temporária e às instruções dos agentes.

articles.body:
Um incêndio atingiu o pátio de uma locadora de veículos no município de Picos , no Piauí, na manhã desta quarta-feira (7). Segundo o gerente da empresa, Alison Moura, mais de 20 carros que estavam parados no local ficaram carbonizados.

Equipes do Corpo de Bombeiros atendem a ocorrência. Não há registro de feridos até a última atualização desta reportagem.

O pátio fica próximo a casas e ruas movimentadas da cidade, como a avenida Beira Rio, e também de uma área de mata, onde supostamente o fogo teria iniciado. Ainda segundo o gerente, alguns dos veículos eram novos.

"Nós não sabe muito bem ainda não (como começou o fogo). Pelo visto, pegou fogo nas redondezas, deve ter voado alguma faísca para dentro e aconteceu o que se consegue ver aí. Pegou fogo em tudo", disse Alison Moura.

articles.title: Feminicídio em Cosmópolis: Justiça decreta prisão preventiva | G1
articles.standfirst: Patrick Silva do Nascimento, tomou veneno após matar Luana Mirela dos Santos Rocha na madrugada desta terça (6). Crianças estavam no imóvel no momento do crime.
articles.summary: Feminicídio em Cosmópolis: Justiça converte em preventiva a prisão de Patrick Silva do Nascimento, que confessou ter matado a companheira a facadas enquanto ela dormia.
articles.body:
A Justiça converteu em preventiva a prisão em flagrante de Patrick Silva do Nascimento, de 30 anos, pelo feminicídio da companheira, Luana Mirela dos Santos Rocha , de 25, em Cosmópolis (SP). A decisão ocorreu após o homem passar por audiência de custódia nesta quarta-feira (7).

O crime aconteceu na residência do casal no bairro Jacinto Raquel Fau na madrugada desta terça-feira. Imagens de câmeras de segurança registraram a chegada da ambulância ao local.

Faca usada no crime foi apreendida pela polícia — Foto: Wesley Justino/EPTV

Patrick confessou o crime à Guarda, alegando que as brigas eram frequentes e que já planejava o homicídio. Ele disse ainda, em primeiro relato aos agentes no hospital, que esperou a vítima dormir para atacá-la com facada no pescoço.

No entanto, durante o interrogatório formal, ele exerceu o direito de permanecer em silêncio.

O homem ingeriu veneno de rato e medicamento anestésico após esfaquear a jovem no pescoço e foi encaminhado para a unidade de saúde, onde foi atendido e permanece sob escolta policial.

Homem preso por feminicídio em Cosmópolis confessou ter planejado matar companheira e esperado vítima dormir para atacá-la com faca em Cosmópolis — Foto: Reprodução/g1 Piracicaba

Luana chegou a ser socorrida e levada ao pronto-socorro, mas não resistiu aos ferimentos e morreu no hospital.

Após o crime, o homem tentou tirar a própria vida ingerindo medicamentos e veneno de rato, sendo encaminhado a uma unidade de saúde.

Luana Mirella dos Santos Rocha morreu após dar entrada em um pronto-socorro com ferimentos causados por faca em Cosmópolis — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Três crianças, de oito, seis e dois anos, estavam na residência no momento do crime. A menina de 2 anos é filha do suspeito. Os dois meninos são enteados dele.

Os menores foram atendidos pelo Conselho Tutelar e ficaram sob os cuidados do avô. A faca utilizada no feminicídio foi apreendida pela polícia e encaminhada para a perícia técnica.

Caso foi registrado da Delegacia de Cosmópolis — Foto: Wesley Justino/EPTV

O crime ocorreu na Rua Ladislau Tallo. A jovem morreu após dar entrada em pronto-socorro de Cosmópolis .

O caso foi atendido pela Guarda Civil. Conforme apurado com os socorristas da ambulância, o homem foi encontrado na calçada do imóvel e a mulher no corredor da residência.

A Guarda Municipal relatou que o quarto do casal apresentava muitas manchas de sangue, evidenciando a violência do crime. Vizinhos relataram à reportagem que o casal brigava muito e mantinha uma convivência reservada com os moradores da região.

articles.title: In 2016, an Arkansas woman put one wooden pantry outside a church with food and toiletries; within three months the idea had gone global, and the movement now maps 2,301 mini pantries
articles.summary: Sometimes an idea for helping people does not begin with a foundation, a fundraiser or a grand plan.
articles.body: Sometimes an idea for helping people does not begin with a foundation, a fundraiser or a grand plan. Sometimes it starts with a small wooden box, a few cans of food and the simple realisation that a neighbourhood can look after its own. In Fayetteville, Arkansas, Jessica McClard was fascinated by the Little Free Library movement, which was bringing tiny book-sharing structures into neighbourhoods. She began wondering whether the same principle could be applied to something more immediate than books. What if people could share food, toiletries and everyday essentials in exactly the same way?In May 2016, that question became the Little Free Pantry and that slowly became a huge success. Scroll down to read this success story.From books to basic needsAccording to ABC News, McClard installed what she believed to be the first Little Free Pantry outside Good Shepherd Lutheran Church in Fayetteville. The small wooden structure was stocked with canned food, personal-care products, paper goods and other necessities. The model was deliberately uncomplicated. People who had something to spare could leave it. Anyone who needed something could take it. There were no forms, membership cards or complicated systems to navigate.The pantry quickly demonstrated how much demand existed for such a simple resource. Items that disappeared particularly quickly included deodorant, toothpaste, toothbrushes, diapers, feminine hygiene products, toilet paper and paper towels. Food remained important, but the experiment also highlighted how expensive everyday necessities can become when household budgets are stretched.A community takes ownershipWhat made the pantry distinctive was not simply what was placed inside it, but what happened around it. As per the same report, people began adding school supplies for children and other useful items. The structure itself became something of a community canvas, with neighbours decorating it for occasions such as Memorial Day. The pantry was no longer just McClard's project. It had begun to belong to the neighbourhood. Handwritten thank-you notes left inside the pantry became another small but meaningful sign of its impact. The reach also extended beyond the immediate area, with people travelling from other places to visit the original pantry.A small idea spreadsThe idea soon travelled beyond Fayetteville and Arkansas, developing into networks of mini pantries in communities across the United States and elsewhere. Some local networks began maintaining their own maps, including the Lowcountry Blessing Box Project and Pātaka Kai Open Street Pantries, adds the official website of Little Free Pantry. The wider movement now maps 2,301 mini pantries, illustrating how a hyper-local experiment can develop into a much broader community-driven network, the website adds.The project has also found connections with wider cultural and charitable initiatives. In 2021, the Little Free Pantry partnered with Celadon Books and the Jane Goodall Institute around the launch of Jane Goodall's The Book of Hope, bringing the idea of everyday community action into a broader conversation about hope and collective responsibility.The power of something smallThe lasting appeal of the Little Free Pantry lies partly in its simplicity. It does not attempt to solve food insecurity through a sweeping programme. Instead, it creates a visible point where one person can help another without ceremony. Its success also reveals something easily overlooked about community support: people do not always need to be told how to help. Sometimes they simply need a place to put their generosity.Image Courtesy: The Chronicle of PhilanthropyYou use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 1934, J.C. Hunter offered 43,200 Texas acres to the US for $237,600; 35 years later, his family's 72,071-acre ranch sold for $1.5 million, forming over 90% of Guadalupe Mountains National Park
articles.summary: What if a piece of land offered to the government for $237,600 had been bought then?
articles.body: What if a piece of land offered to the government for $237,600 had been bought then? The answer might have changed the history of the Guadalupe Mountains by decades. In 1934, Texas rancher J.C. Hunter offered 43,200 acres to the US government, hoping the spectacular mountain country could be protected. The offer went nowhere. More than three decades later, his son, J.C. Hunter Jr., sold the family land to the federal government; this time, 72,071 acres for $1.5 million. According to the National Park Service, the later acquisition accounted for more than 90% of the land that became Guadalupe Mountains National Park.When the mountains were still ranch countryThe Guadalupe Mountains were a very different place in the early 20th century. There was no national park, no network of trails and no stream of visitors arriving to explore the landscape. Much of the area was privately owned ranch land. J.C. Hunter, a rancher from Van Horn, Texas, became particularly interested in the mountains. He had visited McKittrick Canyon and developed an appreciation for the area. At the same time, he was expanding his ranching interests in the region.During the 1920s and 1930s, Hunter put together several smaller ranches, creating what became known as the Guadalupe Mountain Ranch. Sheep and goats were raised on the property, and Hunter worked to provide water for livestock in the higher parts of the ranch. Yet he did not see the mountains only as grazing land. He was also interested in the possibility of protecting them for the future.A major offer came in 1934Hunter's idea took a concrete form in 1934. That year, he offered 43,200 acres to the federal government for $237,600, according to the National Park Service. The property was owned by the Grisham-Hunter Corporation, and the price was based on what the corporation had paid for the land. There was some support for the idea of protecting the area. Roger W. Toll, then superintendent of Yellowstone National Park, had visited the Guadalupe Mountains and discussed the possibility of creating a national park with Hunter. But several things stood in the way.The federal government was not prepared at that time to spend large amounts of money acquiring privately owned land for a new park. The Guadalupe Mountains were also remote, and there was little infrastructure in the area. So Hunter's offer did not result in a park. For the next several decades, the mountains remained part of a working ranch landscape.The ranch passed to J.C. Hunter Jr.When J.C. Hunter died in 1945, the property passed to his son, J.C. Hunter Jr. The younger Hunter continued to expand the ranch. Eventually, the family property covered 72,071 acres. He also retained his father's interest in the mountains and their possible future as protected land. The ranch continued to operate as a ranch, with livestock and wildlife sharing the property. Hunter Jr. also enjoyed the recreational side of the land and welcomed friends to the ranch.Owning tens of thousands of acres, however, came with its own problems. Hunter Jr. was also concerned about the financial burden that could fall on his family, including taxes. Selling the ranch to the government became a possibility again.The second offer was much biggerBy 1966, efforts to acquire Hunter Jr.'s property for the federal government had gained more momentum. This time, the circumstances were different. The idea of creating a national park in the Guadalupe Mountains had gained much more momentum, and the federal government was interested in acquiring the land needed to make it happen. The deal was eventually completed in December 1969. The government bought 72,071 acres from Hunter Jr. for $1.5 million, according to the National Park Service.The figures are striking when placed next to his father's earlier offer. In 1934, J.C. Hunter had offered 43,200 acres for $237,600. Thirty-five years later, his son sold a larger tract for $1.5 million. More importantly, the purchase supplied more than 90% of the land assembled for Guadalupe Mountains National Park.The Hunters were not the only ones involvedThe park's creation was not the work of the Hunter family alone. Wallace Pratt, a petroleum geologist, had become closely associated with McKittrick Canyon. He eventually donated nearly 6,000 acres there to the federal government, adding another important piece to the effort to preserve the Guadalupe Mountains.Congress authorised Guadalupe Mountains National Park in 1966. The Hunter land purchase followed, and the National Park Service continued putting the pieces together. The park was dedicated and opened to the public in September 1972.A working ranch leaves its markToday, visitors know Guadalupe Mountains National Park for its rugged peaks, canyons and desert scenery. But the landscape also carries the history of the ranchers who once owned and worked it. Places such as Frijole Ranch and Williams Ranch preserve pieces of that past. The Hunter family's role stands out because its story unfolded over generations. J.C. Hunter saw the possibility of protecting the mountains in the 1930s. His son eventually helped turn that possibility into a national park.What Hunter could not accomplish with his $237,600 offer in 1934 was ultimately achieved through a much larger transaction decades later: 72,071 acres changing hands for $1.5 million and becoming the foundation of one of Texas's most distinctive national parks.You use AI every day. articles.title: US navy helicopter didn’t crash in Red Sea: CENTCOM fact-checks Iran claim, says all aircraft safe
articles.summary: The US Central Command (CENTCOM) has rejected reports in Iranian state media claiming that a US Navy MH-60R helicopter crashed into the Red Sea after
articles.body: The US Central Command (CENTCOM) has rejected reports in Iranian state media claiming that a US Navy MH-60R helicopter crashed into the Red Sea after declaring an emergency.In a post on X on October 6, CENTCOM fact-checked the claim, saying reports of a downed US Navy helicopter in the Red Sea were false. It also said all US military aircraft and personnel across the Middle East were “safe and accounted for”.What did CENTCOM say about the helicopter?CENTCOM said Iranian state media had been pushing “false reports” that a US Navy MH-60R helicopter crashed in the Red Sea after declaring an emergency the previous night.“Reports of a downed US Navy helicopter in the Red Sea are not true,” CENTCOM said in its post, adding that all US military aircraft and personnel across the Middle East were safe and accounted for.The clarification came after Iranian state media outlets, including Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB), reported that an American naval aircraft operating over the Red Sea had transmitted squawk code 7700, an international transponder signal indicating a general emergency.IRIB had claimed that an MH-60R helicopter belonging to the US Navy crashed in the Red Sea after declaring the emergency code. Iran's Tasnim News Agency also reported that flight-tracking data showed the helicopter flying at an altitude of around 475 feet when the emergency was declared.According to the reports, the helicopter's displayed altitude later dropped to zero before it disappeared from the tracking service. CENTCOM, however, rejected the reports and said there had been no US Navy helicopter crash in the Red Sea.The denial comes amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict and reports of significant US military aircraft losses during the war. A Congressional Research Service report has listed losses involving US planes, drones and helicopters, including an F-35A Lightning II and F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jets.At least 45 MQ-9 Reaper drones have also reportedly been lost during the conflict.Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump has said the war with Iran could end soon, with the outcome depending on whether it happens the “nice way” or the “not-so-nice way”.Speaking in Maryland, Trump said the US was doing “extremely well” in Iran and described the country as the former “bully of the Middle East”.“Our Navy is leading the way in ensuring that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon,” Trump said, reiterating that Iran would not be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday struck a defiant note over the 45 FIRs against him, saying every such FIR is a \"medal\"
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday struck a defiant note over the 45 FIRs against him, saying every such FIR is a "medal" for him and that his "goal is to have 100 FIRs".The Congress leader also stepped up his attack on Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, who has been in the opposition's crosshairs over his functioning and reported dissent among his subordinates.Rahul Gandhi, while declaring an impromptu protest from Jantar Mantar, said, "Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign," and called him an “illegitimate” poll body chief."Our plan is to go to the designated protest site, Jantar Mantar, and sit there together once again, and tell the country that, for us, Gyanesh Kumar is not the legitimate Election Commissioner of the country," he said.The Raebareli Lok Sabha MP attacked Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, alleging that the trio, in cahoots with Gyanesh Kumar have "destroyed the democracy of the country"."Modi Ji, Amit Shah Ji, Mohan Bhagwat, and Gyanesh Kumar have destroyed the democracy of the country. As I said yesterday, those who have done this are traitors to the country, and we will take action against them. I am telling you right now: Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign," the Congress scion claimed.When asked about the FIR against him, he says, "I have 45 FIRs against me. My goal is to have 100. I want 100 FIRs to be registered against me. Every FIR is a medal for me."The opposition has upped the ante against Gyanesh Kumar. On Tuesday, the parties staged a day long protest which culminated in the Rahul Gandhi's detention. The opposition parties are also holding parallel protests across states, with the Congress signalling that the face-off will continue till the CEC resigns.Meanwhile, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leaders and workers were stopped by police personnel at barricades on Wednesday as they staged a protest march from the Sindhi Academy near Kashmere Gate towards the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer’s (CEO) office, alleging widespread "vote theft."Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Turkish opposition stronghold falls in Erdogan's hands as Izmir mayor defects
articles.summary: The mayor of Izmir, a major Turkish city and the secular opposition's stronghold, joined President Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AK Party on Wednesday.
articles.body: The mayor of Izmir, a major Turkish city and the secular opposition's stronghold, joined President Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AK Party on Wednesday.In 2024, Cemil Tugay was elected as the mayor from the Republican People's Party (CHP) before quitting in June. Tugay had won the election with 49 per cent of the vote, defeating the AKP candidate who got a share of 37 per cent.He formally joined the AKP during a ceremony headed by Erdogan in Ankara."I welcome Izmir Mayor Cemil Tugay who is today joining the AKP family," Erdogan told party members in Ankara. AFP reported.The move is being seen as a huge symbolic victory for Erdogan, handing his party the mayoralty of a western coastal city it has never won at the ballot box.Izmir has long been regarded as the heartland of Turkey's secular, social democratic opposition.The defection comes as the opposition battles an increasingly intense crackdown on its mayors and elected officials. Dozens have been jailed pending trial in corruption cases, and observers say the arrests and lawsuits are politically motivated, a charge the opposition also makes. AFP reported.The crackdown followed the CHP's resounding victory in the 2024 local elections, a major blow for Erdogan. Since then, the party has faced a growing intimidation campaign.According to figures published by the independent Diken news website and cited by AFP, six of CHP's provincial mayors have been arrested, including Istanbul mayor Ekrem Imamoglu, along with 29 district mayors, 13 of them in Istanbul.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Russia pursuing deliberate strategy of terror’: EU chief sends €1.24 billion to Ukraine
articles.summary: EU president Ursula von der Leyen said Russia was pursuing a “deliberate strategy of terror” as the European Commission announced it had disbursed €1.24
articles.body: EU president Ursula von der Leyen said Russia was pursuing a “deliberate strategy of terror” as the European Commission announced it had disbursed €1.24 billion ($1.4 billion) to Ukraine for drones, drone interceptors, drone ammunition and missiles.“Russia is pursuing a deliberate strategy of terror. To protect people and infrastructure, Europe is stepping up. Others must step up their support too,” von der Leyen said in a statement.The funding is part of the €90 billion loan facility previously promised by the European Union. The announcement came after Russian missiles and drones struck Kyiv and around a dozen other Ukrainian regions overnight into Wednesday, killing at least 19 civilians, including four children, and injuring around 60, according to Ukrainian officials.Russian strikes kill civilians across UkraineUkraine had anticipated the attack, with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warning a day earlier that intelligence indicated Russia was preparing a “massive” strike.A Russian strike destroyed an apartment block in Pryluky, in the northern Chernihiv region, killing 13 people, including four children, and injuring about 50, Interior Minister Ihor Vyhivskyi said.Deaths were also reported in Kyiv and three other Ukrainian cities. In Kremenchuk, in the Poltava region, two people were killed and seven injured, according to regional officials, while rescue operations continued.“The Russians wanted to strike painfully and demonstratively,” Zelenskyy said on social media.Ukraine is searching worldwide for available Patriot missiles, which are in short supply due to the Iran war. Zelenskyy said Russian ballistic missiles remain the country's biggest air defence challenge.“Russian ballistic missiles remain the greatest challenge. And air defense packages for us right now are a vital necessity,” Zelenskyy said.Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces carried out a massive overnight strike targeting Ukrainian facilities involved in the production and storage of missiles and drones. It also said port and ship-repair facilities in the southern Odesa region and ships carrying cargo for the Ukrainian military were hit.EU prepares fresh sanctions The latest Russian attacks came as EU envoys prepared to approve about 1,650 new designations under the bloc's sanctions regime against Russia. Most of the targets are linked to the country's military-industrial complex.The package, proposed by the EU's foreign policy arm, the EEAS, would be the single largest set of designations since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Once approved by ambassadors, the listings will be sent to EU foreign ministers next Monday for final adoption.Ukraine has also continued long-range strikes inside Russia. Zelenskyy said Ukrainian forces targeted two oil facilities and a training ground in Russia's Perm, Samara and Astrakhan regions using long-range drones and missiles.Russia and Ukraine remain engaged in a long-range aerial war while their armies are largely deadlocked on the battlefield, more than four and a half years after Moscow's full-scale invasion.US-led peace efforts have so far failed to bring short-term relief, with the possibility of low-level technical talks still under discussion. Russian President Vladimir Putin is continuing the invasion, while Western analysts say Moscow is betting that continued pressure will weaken Ukraine and eventually reduce support from its Western allies.You use AI every day. articles.title: Knife attack at Polish school leaves 7 injured; 19-year-old student arrested
articles.summary: Polish police have arrested a 19-year-old man after a knife attack at a vocational school in Ostrołęka, north of Warsaw, left at least seven people
articles.body: Polish police have arrested a 19-year-old man after a knife attack at a vocational school in Ostrołęka, north of Warsaw, left at least seven people injured on Wednesday, according to police and local authorities.The provincial police headquarters said the man was detained after emergency services were called to Vocational School Complex No. 4. Police said the attack took place at around 11am and that the attacker used a “sharp object”.The suspect was a student at the school, police said. He was also wounded when he was arrested and was taken to hospital. Police did not immediately provide details about the severity of his injuries.Ostrołęka mayor Paweł Niewiadomski said authorities had brought the situation under control and were working to establish what had happened.“The most important information is that the situation has been brought under control,” mayor Paweł Niewiadomski said in a statement.He said authorities were at the school seeking to clarify “all the circumstances of the incident”.Police said the seven injured included both students and teachers. Local broadcaster RMF FM reported that most of those wounded were students and that one teacher was among the victims. It also reported that two people had suffered serious injuries.Police later published a photograph on X showing an officer with his hand on the back of a person lying on the ground with their hands tied behind their back. The person's face and hands were pixelated in the image.The incident prompted a major emergency response at the school, while police began an investigation into the circumstances of the attack.School attacks are uncommon in Poland. However, a stabbing at a Catholic convent in south-eastern Poland last month left one person dead and four others injured, according to the report. articles.title: Valkyrae was honoured by a Los Angeles health clinic in 2025 as more than 200 creator-industry leaders helped raise $137,000 for medical care for people in need
articles.summary: Valkyrae was honored by Saban Community Clinic in Los Angeles on Sept. 8, 2025, at its third annual Creators in Action fundraiser.
articles.body: Valkyrae was honored by Saban Community Clinic in Los Angeles on Sept. 8, 2025, at its third annual Creators in Action fundraiser. The streamer, whose real name is Rachell Hofstetter, shared the recognition with pocket.watch founder and CEO, Chris M. Williams. More than 200 leaders from the digital and creator community attended, and the night raised over $137,000 for the clinic, the largest provider of free and reduced-cost healthcare in Los Angeles.Saban picks creators and executives to honor at each gala. 2025's choice from the gaming world co-owns the esports organization 100 Thieves, runs the animation company Hihi Studios and returned to Twitch in January 2025. The money goes toward medical, dental and behavioral health care for low-income and uninsured patients across the city, and the reasons behind the clinic's pick start with a résumé that reaches well past gaming.Why Valkyrae was honored by a Los Angeles health clinic in 2025Creators in Action began in 2023, and Saban Community Clinic uses it to recognize people who have shaped digital media. The first gala honored the duo Rhett & Link and creator-attorney Adam Kaller. In 2024, the clinic recognized Jay Shetty and Malik Ducard, the chief content officer at Pinterest. The 2025 class paired Valkyrae with Williams, which put a gaming voice and a family-content executive on the same program.The clinic built its choices around range. In its announcement, Saban said this year's honorees show innovation, inclusion and influence across entertainment, gaming and digital media. Valkyrae's record fits well. She co-owns 100 Thieves and was named Gaming Creator of the Year by Adweek. She has also won at the Streamy Awards, The Game Awards and the Streamer Awards. In 2024, she launched Hihi Studios, an animation company built to develop original stories rather than only stream them, and her reach as one of the best-known female streamers in the world gave the clinic a name that draws attention.As for Williams, he served as chief audience officer at Maker Studios, and when Disney bought that company in 2014, he moved over to help the studio launch online originals. In 2017, he founded pocket.watch, a developer and distributor of kids and family content that went on to sign deals with Ryan's World, Toys and Colors, and Love Diana.The gala was co-chaired by Brent Weinstein, a senior leader at CAA and a member of the clinic's Friends Board, and Brian Flanagan, president of Mythical Entertainment. Their joint statement explained why the pair stood out. Weinstein and Flanagan said both honorees were shaping entertainment while "using their platforms to uplift others." They added that the influence of Williams and Valkyrae shows creativity can drive real-world change, and that the committee was glad to honor it.The format was simple. Each year the clinic gathers creators and executives from Los Angeles' digital media industry for a cocktail gala, picks honorees from both sides of the business and asks guests to give. Rhett & Link and Kaller in 2023, then Shetty and Ducard in 2024, followed the same creator-plus-executive split that Valkyrae and Williams filled this year.What the $137,000 raised at Creators in Action will fundThe fundraiser took place on Monday, Sept. 8, 2025. Before the event, the clinic said it would be held at the Santa Monica offices of Range Media Partners. Individual tickets started at $150, and sponsorship levels ran from a $500 congratulatory ad up to $15,000.The host committee read like a roster of the creator business. It included Ali Berman, partner and co-head of UTA Creators at United Talent Agency, and Ben Davis, partner and co-head of WME Digital. Lauren Schwartz, an attorney at Hansen, Jacobson, Megan Smith of Align Public Relations, Dan Weinstein of Underscore Talent, Max Cutler of Pave Studios and Rana Zand of Range Media Partners also served, covering law, publicity, talent representation and production.After the night ended, Saban reported that the evening raised more than $137,000. The clinic said the funds will support health services for thousands of Angelenos in need. Its scale explains the stakes. The clinic handles more than 150,000 appointments a year across medical, dental, and behavioral care, and 83% of its patients live below the federal poverty line.Success story: Valkyrae was in Time's 100 creatorsValkyrae made the 2026 list of Time’s 100 most influential creators. Her co-owners at 100 Thieves include Scooter Braun and Drake. She hosts the podcast Wine About It with fellow streamer QTCinderella, has appeared in music videos for Machine Gun Kelly, Willow Smith and The Kid LAROI, and has voiced characters in several animated films.The streamer returned to Twitch in 2025 after her exclusive YouTube deal and was welcomed back with a lot of fanfare. Her followers across Twitch, YouTube and TikTok total 7.9 million.How Valkyrae turned gaming fame into a powerhouse creator careerHofstetter's path started in ordinary jobs. She worked at a bank, a car wash, an arcade, a restaurant and GameStop while attending community college. A gaming Instagram account she began during the GameStop years drew followers who urged her to stream, and she went live on Twitch in 2015. For a while she kept her day jobs, until the money from streaming passed her paychecks and she became a full-time creator.The big jump came in 2018, when 100 Thieves signed her as its first female content creator. In January 2020 she left Twitch for an exclusive YouTube deal. The terms were never made public, and her early streams drew modest crowds. Then the "Among Us" boom arrived. Stream Hatchet counted 23.6 million hours watched for her in 2020, enough to edge past Pokimane as the year's top female streamer, and she won Content Creator of the Year at The Game Awards that December.In April 2021 she and CouRageJD joined the 100 Thieves ownership group. Her work then moved beyond gaming. She co-hosted Netflix's "Inside: USA" with Fanum in 2025 and launched Hihi Studios with media executive Kai Gayoso. Its first original, the webtoon "Bad Influence," came out in 2025.Celebrity Net Worth estimates her net worth at $10 million. Brand deals with HyperX, Gymshark and Alienware, plus a merchandise store, add to income that no longer depends on one platform.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: The backstory: From the 'Promised Land' to October 7 - the origin story of Israel-Palestine conflict
articles.summary: Three years ago, Israel experienced one of the deadliest days in its modern history.
articles.body: Three years ago, Israel experienced one of the deadliest days in its modern history. Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups launched a large-scale attack from Gaza, crossing the border and attacking Israel during a music festival.More than 1,200 people were killed and 251 people were taken hostage on October 7, 2023, according to the United Nations.The attack led Israel to launch a massive attack in Gaza that has since reshaped the region but remains unresolved.So, the question is why conflict resolution is so complicated. The reasons include the history of the two much before October 7, starting with a “promised land”.In modern political and popular discourse, the Jewish connection to the land is said to be going back 3,000 years. The figure refers to the history of the ancient Israelites and the long-standing Jewish religious connection to the land.It all begins with Abraham, a biblical patriarch, and the Jewish belief of the “Promised Land”.Abraham and the 'Promised Land'Abraham is one of the central figures in the Hebrew Bible and is regarded in Jewish tradition as the first of the three patriarchs of the Jewish people, followed by his son Isaac and grandson Jacob. He is also an important figure in Christianity and Islam.According to the Book of Genesis, God tells Abraham to leave his homeland and travel to a land that God will show him. That land is subsequently identified in the biblical account as Canaan, an ancient name for a region encompassing parts of present-day Israel and the Palestinian territories, although biblical descriptions of its boundaries vary.God then promises the land to Abraham's descendants. This becomes the basis of the Jewish concept of the “Promised Land”.For all the land which thou seest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed for ever.The biblical story continues through Abraham's son Isaac and grandson Jacob, who is given the name Israel. Thus, Jacob's descendants became known as the ‘Children of Israel’.However, the biblical Land of Israel and the modern State of Israel are not the same thing.The modern State of Israel was established only in 1948. The biblical story belongs to an ancient religious tradition dating back thousands of years.For centuries, however, the land remained central to Jewish religious memory. Even after Jews were dispersed across different parts of the world, prayers and religious traditions continued to focus on Jerusalem and the Land of Israel.Ancient homeland to modern political ideaFor centuries, the Jewish connection to the Land of Israel remained deeply rooted in religion, history and identity. Even after Jewish communities were dispersed across different parts of the world, Jerusalem and the land remained central to Jewish religious memory and prayer.By the late 19th century, that ancient connection began to take on a modern political form. Zionism emerged in Europe as a movement seeking Jewish national self-determination and a homeland for Jews, amid growing antisemitism and persecution.And the territory at the centre of that movement was Palestine, which encompassed much of the land Jews regarded as their historic homeland.But Palestine was not an empty land waiting for a new population. It was home to a predominantly Arab population, including Muslims and Christians, as well as a longstanding Jewish community.As Jewish immigration increased, particularly from Europe, two national movements increasingly came to see the same territory as their homeland: the Zionist movement seeking a Jewish national home, and Palestinian Arabs seeking political self-determination in the land where they lived.That claim to the same territory would become the central question of the conflict that followed.1917: Britain promises a Jewish national homeThe First World War transformed the region.At the time, Palestine was part of the Ottoman Empire. During the war, Britain fought the Ottoman Empire and eventually took control of the territory.In 1917, Britain issued the Balfour Declaration, expressing support for the establishment in Palestine of a “national home for the Jewish people”. At the same time, the declaration said that nothing should be done to prejudice the civil and religious rights of the existing non-Jewish communities in Palestine.For the Zionist movement, the declaration was a major diplomatic breakthrough.For the Arab population of Palestine, however, the prospect of a Jewish national home in a territory where they were already the majority gave rise to concerns and opposition.Britain subsequently governed Palestine under a League of Nations mandate. Jewish immigration increased, while relations between Jewish and Arab communities became increasingly tense and violent.1947: The UN proposes two statesAfter the Holocaust and the devastation of European Jewry during World War II, international support for a Jewish state grew.Britain eventually handed the Palestine question to the newly established United Nations.In 1947, the UN proposed partitioning Palestine into two independent states - one Jewish and one Arab. Jerusalem was to be placed under a special international regime because of its importance to Jews, Muslims and Christians.Jewish leaders accepted the partition plan but Arab Palestinian leaders and Arab states rejected it.The dispute soon turned into war.1948: Israel is born, Palestinians experience the NakbaOn May 14, 1948, David Ben-Gurion, the head of the Jewish Agency and leader of the Jewish community in Palestine, declared the establishment of the State of Israel and became its first prime minister.The next day, armies from neighbouring Arab states entered the conflict, beginning the first Arab-Israeli war.Israel not just survived the war but ended up controlling considerably more territory than the Jewish state envisaged under the UN partition plan. The Palestinian Arab state proposed by the UN was never established.For Palestinians, it meant that more than half of the Palestinian Arab population fled or were expelled., becoming refugees. Palestinians refer to this mass displacement and dispossession as the Nakba, or “catastrophe”.Thus, many Palestinians and their descendants continue to demand the right to return to homes and properties from which they were displaced, while Palestinian national politics increasingly came to centre on self-determination and statehood.1967: The land question becomes even more complicatedAnother major turning point came nearly two decades later.During the Six-Day War in 1967, Israel captured the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza, along with other territories. The war brought another major displacement of Palestinians and placed the territories at the centre of the conflict that followed.For Palestinians, the West Bank and Gaza became central to their demand for an independent state, while East Jerusalem became a particularly important part of their national and religious claim. The occupation also meant that about 1.2 million Palestinians came under Israeli military control, as per UN's historical account.Israel's government and different political and religious groups have had varying positions on the status of the West Bank, with parts of Israeli society viewing the territory through the biblical and historical framework of “Judea and Samaria”, the biblical and historical names for the area now commonly known internationally as the West Bank.Israeli settlements were subsequently established in the occupied territories. The settlement issue became one of the most contentious subjects in Israeli-Palestinian negotiations. The UN continues to refer to the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, as occupied Palestinian territory.This is where the ancient idea of the Promised Land intersects most visibly with the modern conflict.So where does October 7 fit into this historyBy October 7, 2023, the conflict had already passed through major wars in 1948, 1967 and 1973, as well as two Palestinian uprisings known as the Intifadas.There had also been the Oslo peace process, the split between Hamas and the Palestinian Authority, and repeated rounds of fighting between Israel and Hamas.At the heart of the unresolved conflict were longstanding disputes over territory, Israeli settlements, Jerusalem, Palestinian refugees, borders and the creation of a Palestinian state.Then came the Hamas-led attack on Israel three years ago. Israel subsequently launched its war in Gaza.Three years later, October 7 remains the defining date of the current conflict.However, as explained, the actual conflict started much before.Why does the ‘Promised Land’ still matterThe phrase helps explain why the land itself carries such deep meaning.However, coming back to October 7 and the subsequent conflict, it cannot be explained simply as a religious fight over the land promised to Abraham. The backdrop comes from there but the conflict is the result of several layers of modern history. These include the rise of nationalism, European antisemitism and Jewish immigration, the British Mandate, the Holocaust, the creation of Israel and the displacement of Palestinians.The “Promised Land” is therefore the beginning of the backstory, not the whole story.Still, to understand why the conflict has proved so difficult to end, one has to understand something that predates both Israel and Palestine as modern political entities.You use AI every day. articles.title: US marines in Japan face month-long curfew, alcohol ban amid probe of woman’s murder
articles.summary: US Marines stationed on Japan’s Okinawa island have been placed under a month-long curfew and banned from consuming alcohol following the arrest of a
articles.body: US Marines stationed on Japan’s Okinawa island have been placed under a month-long curfew and banned from consuming alcohol following the arrest of a Marine accused of murdering a Japanese woman.The US Forces in Okinawa also suspended military operations for 48 hours from Wednesday to conduct training on standards and discipline, Reuters reported. Personnel have been restricted from leaving their bases for social activities during the period.Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, is suspected of killing Anna Yagi, 39, at a hotel in Naha, the capital of Okinawa, on Saturday. Police said Ballard allegedly took the woman’s wallet and backpack. He has dismissed the allegations.US military officials said the measures were aimed at reinforcing discipline and rebuilding trust with the local community. “Every interaction with our neighbors either builds or undermines the trust” essential to the alliance, Lt Gen Benjamin Watson said in a statement.‘Brutal and heinous’Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi described the killing as “extremely brutal and heinous” and said Tokyo had strongly protested to the US over the incident. She called for measures to prevent similar cases in the future.Police said Yagi died of asphyxiation after Ballard allegedly pressed on her neck, according to Stars and Stripes. Hotel staff found her unconscious in her room after she failed to check out.Local media reported that around 200 police officers were involved in the search for Ballard after CCTV showed him entering the hotel with Yagi.The killing has renewed concerns in Okinawa over the large US military presence on the island, which has long been a source of tension among residents over noise, aircraft accidents and alleged misconduct by military personnel.Japan hosts the largest overseas contingent of US forces, with most of the roughly 18,000 US Marines stationed in Okinawa. The US controlled the island from the end of World War II until 1972.The latest incident could also complicate efforts to relocate some Marines from the crowded Futenma air base to a facility at Henoko. Okinawa, located about 100 km from Taiwan at its closest point, is considered strategically important by Japan and the US for deterring potential Chinese military action in the region.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi grew livid after she was prevented, along with the rest of the party workers, from marching towards Jantar Mantar and lambasted the government over its handling of the opposition protest against Election Commission chief Gyanesh Kumar.“Is this the way? You can see what they are doing,” Priyanka said shortly before she was forcefully bundled into the police bus amid high-voltage drama.“This is how they treat Members of Parliament (MPs) who are asking simply to meet the Election Commissioner. This is how they treat us. They are beating MPs. The policemen have scratched me all over. They have thrown us to the ground. Now, we are not going to move from here. Let them bring their forces back. I will not move from here,” she was quoted as saying by news agency ANI.Before she was detained, Priyanka lay down in the middle of a road packed with protesters and security personnel, alleging that cops had “scratched her all over” and “thrown” her to the ground.As Priyanka was lying down, Congress and INDIA bloc leaders encircled her, along with Rahul Gandhi, to prevent cops from getting close to her. However, soon after, Rahul was picked up and detained.Congress MP Charanjit Singh Channi said, “We want to go towards the ECI office; this government has resorted to hooliganism. There is no democracy...We are being stopped.”"It is our democratic right; we are fighting for this right. Article 19 grants us permission to protest in this manner, and Jantar Mantar is a designated spot; if we cannot stage a protest here, then where else can we do it?... We are fighting for our rights—fighting for the rights of the country's voters—yet every time, we are being stopped in this struggle. We are being prevented from even entering this designated protest site, Jantar Mantar; Members of Parliament are being stopped from entering...It is not the Delhi Police's fault; their boss is a coward," Congress leader and Rajya Sabha MP Pawan Khera said.As he got off the bus of INDIA bloc MPs, RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha said, “This is a launch. Not just Gyanesh Kumar; this Government is going out now. They are launching a lathi charge on the soul of India, on the democracy of India. Shame on such people.”Kumari Selja, AICC General Secretary and Congress Uttarakhand in-charge, said, “An institution that ought to be the guardian of our Constitution and our democracy—today, it seems the guardian itself has become the predator. The Election Commission—or rather, the Chief Election Commissioner—bears significant blame for the clouds of suspicion hovering over our democracy and the threats to its survival,” she said.CPM MP John Brittas said, “Malayali, Kashmiri, everyone is here. Everyone is united to bring down Gyanesh Kumar. We are all together.”Just hours earlier, Rahul Gandhi had stepped up his attack on Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, who has been in the Opposition's crosshairs over his functioning and reported dissent among his subordinates.Rahul Gandhi, declaring that he would launch a fresh protest from Jantar Mantar, said, “Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign,” and called him an “illegitimate” poll body chief.“Our plan is to go to the designated protest site, Jantar Mantar, and sit there together once again, and tell the country that, for us, Gyanesh Kumar is not the legitimate Election Commissioner of the country,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Recuperating well': MEA provides health update on hero pilot Captain Smit Machchhar
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Captain Smit Machchhar, the Indian pilot injured in a mid-air attack on a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight, is “recuperating well” and responding
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Captain Smit Machchhar, the Indian pilot injured in a mid-air attack on a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight, is “recuperating well” and responding positively to treatment, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Tuesday.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Machchhar remains hospitalised in Abu Dhabi, with the Indian embassy in the UAE maintaining regular contact with him, his family and local authorities.“Captain Smit Machchhar is in the hospital in Abu Dhabi. Our embassy in the UAE has been in regular touch with him, with his family, with local authorities, and with the hospital authorities. He's recuperating well. He's responding well. And his health is improving,” Jaiswal said.The update came after the Indian Embassy in the UAE said Machchhar was making “steady progress” and “regaining his health”. The pilot suffered severe injuries to his head, neck and hand after co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national, attacked him during the flight and attempted to take control of the aircraft.Machchhar's condition had become critical during the incident, with heavy bleeding from his injuries and his pulse dropping dangerously low. He was kept stable during the flight by Dr Shuta Musaev, a Georgian dentist living in Israel who was the only doctor on board.Musaev told ABC News that he used T-shirts as pressure dressings and ice packs to control the bleeding for around 45 minutes. At one point, Machchhar's pulse became dangerously low and Musaev raised his feet until his pulse recovered.“When I saw his lips were blue, I told the steward, 'We need to land quickly. He doesn’t have much more time',” Musaev said.Machchhar was eventually handed over to medical teams after the aircraft landed in Saudi Arabia. He has since been receiving treatment in the UAE.The pilot has been hailed as a “hero” by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for his actions during the attack. Musaev also credited Machchhar with helping save the lives of those on board.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Russia pushes back on plague fears, says no epidemic risk after death of Siberian lab worker
articles.summary: Russia’s health watchdog on Wednesday said there was no epidemic risk to people in the eastern Siberian Irkutsk region following the death of a worker at
articles.body: Russia’s health watchdog on Wednesday said there was no epidemic risk to people in the eastern Siberian Irkutsk region following the death of a worker at a plague research institute, while the Kremlin said Moscow had properly informed the World Health Organization (WHO) about the case.According to news agency Reuters, regulator Rospotrebnadzor said medical monitoring of people who had contact with the deceased worker, along with laboratory tests, had found no signs of infection or dangerous pathogens.“Preventive and anti-epidemic measures have been organised in full, and there are no epidemic risks for the population of Irkutsk or Irkutsk region,” it said in a statement.The watchdog also said it had shared information about the situation with the WHO. Authorities had quarantined dozens of people after the laboratory worker fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances.Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia had informed the WHO about the death last week in line with established procedures, and accused the media of spreading false information.Peskov was responding to an ABC News report that the United States had lodged a formal diplomatic complaint over Russia’s handling of the case and had urged Moscow to provide greater transparency.“Much of the reporting surrounding the incident was false,” Peskov said, urging people to rely on information released by Rospotrebnadzor.A state television station in Irkutsk reported that she died on October 2 at a hospital in Shelekhov, a town on the outskirts of Irkutsk. Officials have quarantined the hospital and are monitoring people who came into contact with the worker.On Tuesday, the watchdog said no cases of plague had been detected among people who had come into contact with the deceased.WHO director-general Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on Wednesday that Russian authorities had reported no case of plague in the region. WHO had earlier described the possible risk outside Russia as “very low”, while Russian authorities cited a “typical” acute respiratory viral infection.The case has revived memories of the COVID-19 pandemic and earlier disputes over the origins of the virus. Pneumonic plague affects the lungs and can spread between people through respiratory particles, while bubonic plague is more commonly transmitted through infected flea bites.Earlier, US secretary of state Marco Rubio urged Moscow to share more information.“Maybe there’s nothing there. Maybe it’s bigger than we thought. We don’t know,” Rubio said in Iceland, on Tuesday.“We encourage Russia to be more transparent and share more information with the world,” he added, saying the information available so far had been “quite limited”.You use AI every day.
