articles.title: HC refuses interim relief to EV Velu, son in lake illegal lake soil excavation case
articles.summary: Madras High Court denied interim protection to DMK MLA E V Velu and son in DVAC probe over alleged illegal lake soil excavation causing Rs 8.22 crore loss.
articles.body: Chennai: Madras high court on Wednesday refused to direct the DVAC from taking any coercive action against former minister and DMK MLA E V Velu and his son E V Kumaran in connection with a case registered against them for allegedly causing a loss of Rs 8.22 crore to the Tamil Nadu govt by illegally excavating soil from a lake for a DMK Youth Wing conference in Tiruvannamalai.Justice V Lakshminarayanan instead directed the DVAC to file its response to the plea moved by Velu and his son seeking to quash the case by Nov 6. “The Supreme Court has categorically said that the high courts must refrain from passing such interim orders in quash petitions,” the judge said.On Dec 14, DMK‘s north zone youth wing conference was held in Tiruvannamalai. To level the conference venue, soil was allegedly illegally excavated from the nearby Malappambadi Lake, covering an area of 12 acres and a depth ranging from 10 to 23 feet causing Rs 8 crore loss to the govt.Denying the allegations, advocate Rahul Balaji for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners was neither the applicant for the conference nor its organiser. The conference was organised by a Member of Parliament, and the authorities were aware of this.Contending that the provisions invoked in the complaint itself were questionable, he pointed out that the offences included criminal breach of trust and cheating did not arise from the facts alleged.The counsel further submitted that the conference venue was owned by a private limited company and had been used several times previously for holding large conferences. At least three conferences had allegedly been conducted at the same venue earlier.“The authorities were attempting to connect a permission granted for excavation of a small quantity of silt with the allegation that material had subsequently been removed from the lakebed in large quantities. articles.title: First cannon firing drill for Dasara elephants held
articles.summary: First Dasara cannon firing drill in Mysuru acclimatises 13 elephants and 43 mounted police horses; 21 shots fired, more rehearsals set for Oct 9 and 12.
articles.body: Mysuru: The first cannon firing drill to acclimatise the Dasara jumbos and Mounted Police horses to the deafening sound of cannon shots, which will be traditionally fired during the gun salute to Goddess Chamundeshwari during the Dasara procession, was held successfully at Dasara Exhibition Grounds on Wednesday.All the thirteen Dasara jumbos and 43 horses of Mounted Police took part in the cannon drill. From seven cannons 21 cannon shots were fired for three rounds during the event.During the drill, Dasara jumbos and horses remained calm and responded successfully without causing any disturbance. Initially, Dasara elephant Srirama was disturbed but adjusted later. articles.title: AP high court seeks Centre's response on iron ore mine allocation for RINL
articles.summary: AP High Court seeks detailed responses from Centre and Andhra Pradesh officials on pending captive iron ore mine allocation for RINL/Visakhapatnam Steel Plant.
articles.body: Vijayawada: The high court on Wednesday sought detailed responses from the Centre and state authorities on the alleged failure of allotting captive iron ore mines to Visakhapatnam Steel Plant (RINL), a demand that has remained pending for several years.The court was hearing a PIL filed by Steel Plant Employees Union general secretary J Ayodhya Ramu, seeking directions to consider RINL’s request and reserve available iron ore deposits in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh for the steelmaker under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Act.The petitioner also sought a decision on a proposal made by the Union steel ministry on Dec 19, 2019, and a subsequent report submitted by RINL.Senior counsel A Satya Prasad, appearing for the petitioner, told the high court that the demand for captive iron ore mines had remained unresolved despite an earlier high court direction. He said the high court had in 2013 directed the authorities to consider RINL’s request, but no decision had been taken so far.Appearing for the Centre, counsel P Sriram questioned the maintainability of the PIL and sought time to place further details before the court.Considering the submissions on both sides, the HC bench comprising Chief Justice Lisa Gill and Justice Challa Gunaranjan kept the maintainability objection open and directed the Union ministries of steel and mines, state chief secretary, principal secretary for mines, director of mines, AP Mineral Development Corporation managing director, and RINL CMD to file counters with complete details before the next date of hearing.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Vijayawada | Silver Rate in Vijayawada | Bank Holidays in Vijayawada | Public Holidays in Vijayawada | Petrol Price in Vijayawada | Diesel Price in Vijayawada | CNG Price in Vijayawada | LPG Price in VijayawadaStay updated with the latest Vijayawada news. articles.title: New Sanganer Road families pack up as demolition fear becomes reality
articles.summary: Families and traders along Jaipur’s New Sanganer Road begin shifting belongings after Supreme Court rejects stay and JDA demolition action nears.
articles.body: Jaipur: New Sanganer Road looked less like a market than a corridor of half-packed lives on Wednesday morning.From Sodala to Gurjar ki Thadi, shop shutters were pulled up not for business but to drag out sewing machines, cartons, deity frames, school bags and steel trunks.Supreme Court has rejected a stay petition filed by affected residents and traders and the high court has not granted protection against JDA notices. That uncertainty has become an order.Manju Sharma (48) stood inside her garment shop, pointing to chalk marks on the wall. Her in-laws, she said, have lived in the two-storey building for more than 60 years. She has run the shop on the ground floor for over 20 years.“JDA has marked around 28 feet from the road as encroachment, but our house itself is only 26 feet wide,” Sharma said. “That means nothing will remain. We paid more than Rs 3 lakh as civic tax to Jaipur Municipal Corporation this year. Now we are carrying our home away in bags.”Her family has rented a small apartment in Vaishali Nagar and begun shifting utensils, clothes and documents.A little ahead, Anupama Meena’s family had already sent some belongings to their native village in Dausa. Their tailoring shop runs from the front portion of the house. After demolition, they say, Dausa may become their only address.“We were rehabilitated here after my in-laws were removed from the railway station area in the 1970s,” Meena said. “After 50 years, we are refugees again.
